input.body:
You said the review permits **anyone meeting a written public-eye test**, and asks for a **prominent detection disclaimer** and **named-source attribution on every quote**. All three change what the product does, not just what it says. **Twelve images are the review here.** Eleven moved, one is new. ## The test is now a rule, not a series of judgements If the written test is the gate, the test has to exist as one thing. `data/roster.json` now states an `inclusionRule` — written once, applying to everybody — and each entry says how its person meets it. **A file missing either half is refused**, not warned about: > אנחנו עוקבים אחרי מי שהעמיד את עצמו מרצונו בעין הציבור, ורק בתפקיד שבו עשה זאת… איננו עוקבים אחרי אנשים פרטיים, ואיננו אוספים פעילות אישית של אף אחד — כולל של מי שכן נמצא ברשימה. That last clause is deliberate: the boundary applies to people *on* the roster too, not only to those off it. `1.16` grew to cover both halves rather than gaining a near-duplicate sibling — the entry's `qualifies` alone was the old requirement, and it is no longer sufficient. ## Every displayed quote names its publication The figure timeline and search results carried a *count*; the home page carried nothing. A quote with no visible publisher is our word for what somebody said, and one click away is not beside it. `6.13` walks all three surfaces and fails if any shows a quote without a publisher named next to it. Where three outlets carried one utterance, **all three are named** — not one of them, and not a number. Which outlets carried something is part of the record. ## The caveat is where the claim is made `6.6` had it on the methodology page with every finding linking there. That is one click too many for the sentence that matters most: a reader who has just been shown that a named person contradicted themselves is precisely the reader least likely to go looking for the qualification. `6.12` puts it on the finding page, in its own block — the rationale is what the model *said*, the caveat is what the model *cannot know*, and the case asserts they stay separate rather than one absorbing the other. ## One route, not two `GET /api/v1/roster` returns the test and the people together. Two fetches for one page is a page that can render half of itself, and half is wrong in both directions — the test alone reads as a policy nobody applied, the people alone as a list somebody chose. `5.13` asserts both keys arrive or neither does.
